top.description: East Hampton girls soccer players Ava Ploszay (left) and Liv Correia after the Bellringers won the Shoreline Conference championship 1-0 over Old Saybrook at Valley Regional High School in Deep River Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. If you guessed East Hampton, give yourself a round of applause. The team is currently 17-0-0, having gone through the Shoreline Conference regular season and league tournament unscathed. The Bellringers entered the CIAC tournament ranked No. 1 in the Class M/S coaches poll , which was based on regular-season results, and No. 8 in the GametimeCT power rankings . "We obviously felt like, although we've had a good season, we need to take every game as serious as we possibly can because nobody is just going to hand anything to us," junior midfielder Ava Ploszay said. East Hampton will try to extend its streak Tuesday as the top seed in the CIAC Class M tournament against No. 17 Lakeview in a second-round home game at 2 p.m. The perfect record is a byproduct of the cohesive unit the Bellringers have had. As head coach Andrea Giuliano has indicated, this has been building for two seasons. Last year, East Hampton also went through the regular season without a loss, but did have two ties. But you are remembered for how you performed in the postseason. The Bellringers reached the Shoreline Conference final and fell to Valley Regional. They reached the Class M semifinals and lost to eventual champion Foran. A very good season, but not what East Hampton was looking for. We really wanted it, and we knew that no one was going to give it to us, so we had to come out and work really hard." And East Hampton made it back to the Shoreline final this season. Giuliano said her team "came in with a little bit of a chip on our shoulders this game." The Bellringers pitched their 13th shutout of the season in a 1-0 win against Old Saybrook , earning their first conference crown since 2006. Giuliano called starting center backs Abigail Hambidge and Quinn Rurka two of the team's top players. top.title: How Eagles can use their growing collection of premium NFL draft picks
top.description: The Eagles have created options with their draft capital. What they do with those options will determine whether their deadline decisions improve the organization. Following the Jordan Davis agreement, Philadelphia holds five first-round picks and five second-round picks across the next three drafts, according to Jeff McLane’s reported inventory. That matches Adam Schefter’s total of 10 selections in the first two rounds. The collection gives Howie Roseman several paths. None requires announcing a target, predicting a specific draft position, or deciding today how to use every pick. Make multiple selections at premium positions The most direct approach is to draft players. Multiple early selections let Philadelphia address more than one need without relying on later-round prospects to fill immediate openings. The Eagles can evaluate offensive line, defensive line, and other positions based on available talent. Their draft capital should support that evaluation rather than force a predetermined shopping list. Selecting well also creates the possibility of productive players on rookie contracts, helping balance spending elsewhere. Move within a draft when the value supports it Additional selections let Philadelphia move up for a player it values or move down when another team offers worthwhile compensation. That flexibility should not become a trade requirement. Keeping a selection can be the best decision when a strong prospect remains available. The important advantage is having alternatives when the board develops differently than expected. Trade for an established contributor Premium picks can acquire players with an NFL track record. That may become attractive if Philadelphia identifies a specific roster weakness and believes the player’s age, contract, and performance fit its competitive plans. The cost includes more than the pick. An established acquisition can require a substantial contract, limiting the financial advantage of retaining draft choices. Any such move should be tied to a defined need and a realistic assessment of the roster. Spread investment across several years Philadelphia’s early selections are distributed across 2027, 2028, and 2029. That allows the organization to address needs as they evolve rather than concentrating every decision in one offseason. Draft First-round picks Second-round picks 2027 2 1 2028 2 2 2029 1 2 The Eagles do not need to solve every future question with the next available pick. Keep the focus on development Acquiring selections is only part of roster building. Philadelphia must create an environment in which those players can improve, earn responsibilities, and become dependable starters. The Davis trade increased flexibility. It did not guarantee the next successful roster. That will require disciplined decisions, effective coaching, and patience with players whose development will not follow a straight line. top.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
top.description: …As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024. Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August. The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent. The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line. The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August. Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August. Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent. However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August. Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none. The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter. Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators. top.title: Laura Stegall taught her daughter to play volleyball - and a lot more about how to fight
top.description: INDIANAPOLIS — Laura Stegall is somewhere amid the sea of blue that's overtaken half the lower bowl at Gainbridge Fieldhouse Saturday night. She's sporting blue-and-white checkered overalls, celebrating the now three-time defending Class 4A state champion Fort Wayne Carroll volleyball team's four-set win over Center Grove with her son, Brady. Down on the floor, Laura's daughters — senior outside hitter Sarah and freshman setter Ashtyn — are posing for a photo with their dad, Carroll assistant athletic director Randy Stegall. Sarah credits both her parents with "setting the standard" in her life. But her love for volleyball was inspired by Laura, who was a two-sport athlete at Indiana Purdue Fort Wayne (basketball), then launched college volleyball programs at Indiana Tech and Daytona State (Fla.). Laura was Sarah's first coach, the one who taught the Notre Dame commit everything she knows. The two text about the sport on a near-daily basis, Sarah says. "She gets a message before every game, whether she wants it or not," Laura adds in a separate interview. My mom wants the best for me, to make sure I'm always playing with confidence, Sarah explains from outside Gainbridge, the blue championship medal draped around her neck and Laura standing proudly alongside her. The odds were stacked against Laura living to see her oldest child reach high school, let alone play out her senior season. Laura was diagnosed with late-stage ovarian cancer in February 2019. She was given a 39% chance of living five years and a 20% of making it a decade. "But by the grace of God, I'm here eight years later," Laura said in a phone interview with IndyStar last week. Sarah was her family's bedrock while her mother underwent cancer treatments. Just nine years old at the time, she took charge at home, cooking meals and looking after her siblings so Laura could rest while Randy, a college baseball coach at the time, was on the road. "Sarah's truly one of the most responsible, mature people and she stepped up so majorly for our family," Laura says before being overwhelmed by her emotions. "That's a lot to ask of a 9-year-old: 'Hey, I need you to do this for your brother. I need you to cook dinner,' but Sarah stepped up — and she still cooks better than me." Laura takes a moment to collect herself, then reflects on one of her favorite sports memories with Sarah, a swim meet back when the family still lived in Florida. Laura had recently completed cancer treatments and was in attendance to see her 10-year old daughter break a 28-year old breaststroke record. It was a "euphoric moment," she says, her pride beaming through the phone. "And every little benchmark along the way. … I'm sitting there watching Sarah like, 'I'm so grateful to be here to see this.'" 'Mom, are you gonna die?' In an interview with Sky Sport, the Italian praised Marquez's performance, while expressing regret that his own factory - despite delivering its best-ever season in the premier class - has been unable to secure the riders' championship. When asked whether Marquez won the title or Aprilia lost it, Rivola replied: "Marc Marquez won it. Honestly, he was the deciding factor. top.description: Jim Harbaugh © Imagn. The Los Angeles Chargers remain winless after eight games as questions grow around head coach Jim Harbaugh. The Chargers lost to the Houston Texans, 44-22, last week, extending their losing streak to 11 games and dropping to 0-8. NFL analyst John Middlekauff claimed that Harbaugh has lost the locker room’s confidence after last week’s humiliating loss. On his podcast 3 & OUT with John Middlekauff , the analyst compared Harbaugh with former Chargers head coach Brandon Staley, who was fired in his third season. “1, 2, 3, trade me, please. 1, 2, 3, we quit. 1, 2, 3, this is worse than Brandon Staley,” Middlekauff said. “If Jim Harbaugh’s name was Jim Middlekauff, I think he probably would’ve already been fired. Like, this feels bigger than him. This feels, like, organizationally, you know, as Jim lost it, which is crazy to say, but it feels like overnight, like he got no pulse on his team and they’ve quit on him.” Given everything that has unraveled this season for the Chargers, Middlekauff is not sure about any player ahead of the trade deadline. “I know they’ve been adamant, we’re not trading anybody. top.title: NBA fans in Texas could attend Monday’s Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks games for less than $15
top.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Over the years, there have been a lot of complaints about the rising cost of attending an NBA game, but fans in Texas were offered incredible get-in prices for Monday’s slate of games. With three NBA teams, Texas is the state that boasts the second-most franchises, only behind California with four. All three teams have exciting, big-name superstars and playoff aspirations. But you would never know that, going by the ticket prices they were charging for games on Monday night. Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks had incredibly low get-in prices for Monday night games According to data from TickPick , the Houston Rockets vs. Denver Nuggets had a staggeringly low get-in price of just $10 hours before tip-off. As for the Dallas Mavericks, who hosted the Indiana Pacers (albeit without Tyrese Haliburton), they offered fans a get-in price of just $14. These get-in ticket prices actually cost less than the average cost of a six-wing meal combo at WingStop, which only goes to show how affordable the deal was for fans. And while going through first- or third-party ticketing platforms would have added some fees to the overall price of the order, NBA fans in Texas would still be getting a very good deal given the average price of NBA tickets elsewhere in the country and the superstars that were playing. The get-in price of the Rockets vs. Nuggets game is especially surprising, as it boasted two all-time great superstars in Nikola Jokic and Kevin Durant. With a superstar pairing that boasts four MVPs, three NBA championships, and three Finals MVPs between them, you would imagine the demand for tickets would be much higher. And on top of that, both teams are seen as possible contenders, with the Rockets currently on one of their best starts to an NBA season in recent memory. As for the Dallas Mavericks, while they were playing an Indiana Pacers team that is heavily depleted following the loss of Tyrese Haliburton due to injury, their own star pairing of Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg should have been enough to demand a higher get-in price for their game on Monday night. Fans that grabbed tickets at these low prices will be grateful, as it is unlikely that such star-studded teams will get to play again at such a low price again this season. Microsoft teaches schools that free email was just a phase
top.description: Microsoft is retiring its free education email service, leaving schools, colleges, and universities facing new licensing bills if they want to keep students' mailboxes. The company announced plans last week to retire Office 365 A1, the Student Use Benefit program, and free Exchange Online for Alumni. The changes generally take effect at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Office 365 A1 provides eligible institutions with web-based Office applications, Teams, and email at no charge. Its replacement, Microsoft 365 Education A0, excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also depends on paid faculty licensing and students actively using Windows devices for education. A spokesperson for the UK's Department for Education told The Register : "We are disappointed that Microsoft has made this decision. However, we are pleased to have successfully negotiated some additional concessions for the UK, giving schools, colleges and universities the time they need to be able to successfully transition to new licensing agreements." An industry insider said the loss of free Microsoft-hosted email could add thousands to institutions' bills. Another organization noted "significant concerns… around affordability, equitable treatment across the sector, and the longer-term implications of the changes." A spokesperson for UK education technology body Jisc told The Register that its "focus has been on ensuring that UK education providers are well supported and have sufficient time to assess their options." "We continue working closely with Microsoft and sector partners to support those discussions and help institutions make informed decisions about their future requirements." Also being retired are free Exchange Online for Alumni - which lets graduates retain their mailboxes - and the Student Use Benefit, providing student licenses at no additional charge when institutions purchase qualifying faculty licenses. Microsoft plans a paid alumni replacement. The Windows giant is also changing storage entitlements and introducing Microsoft 365 Education A7, its "most advanced education offering," which adds AI, security, governance, and device-management features. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s active telecom lines hit 200m as 5G share crosses 5%
nigeria.description: …As Internet data usage falls to 1.73 terabytes in September By Juliet Umeh Nigeria’s active telecommunications subscriptions rose to 200.3 million in September, crossing the 200 million mark for the first time since the NIN-SIM enforcement exercise led to mass line disconnections in 2024. Latest data from the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, showed that active lines increased by about 2.9 million, from 197.4 million in August. The September figure of 200,337,097 subscriptions was up from 197,416,694 in August. Teledensity rose to 92.41 per cent from 91.07 per cent. The NCC defines teledensity as the number of active telephone connections per 100 inhabitants. It measures subscriptions rather than unique users, as one person may have more than one line. The data showed that 4G remained the largest share of mobile connections at 54.37 per cent in September. 2G accounted for 36.42 per cent, while 3G made up 4.16 per cent. 5G’s share increased to 5.05 per cent from 4.92 per cent in August. Internet subscriptions also grew, rising to 160.9 million from 158.5 million in August. Broadband subscriptions increased to 128 million in September from 126.2 million the previous month, while broadband penetration rose to 59.05 per cent from 58.22 per cent. However, total internet data usage declined to 1.73 million terabytes in September from 1.76 million terabytes in August. Mobile number porting increased during the month, with 1,603 subscribers switching networks, compared with 1,111 in August. MTN recorded 854 incoming ports, Airtel 580, Globacom 165 and Vitel four. T2 recorded none. The figures also showed that the telecommunications industry’s contribution to gross domestic product, GDP, rose to 9.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 9.19 per cent in the first quarter. Fixed broadband infrastructure expanded, with Fibre to the X (FTTX) subscriptions rising to 401,666 in the third quarter from 319,735 in the second quarter. The NCC’s FTTX category covers fibre connections to homes, offices, streets, hubs and other locations, including subscriptions from internet service providers and fixed or private network operators. nigeria.title: UFC chief declines Trump’s White House job offer
nigeria.description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump’s — apparently jovial — offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday that he had asked White to take on the high-profile post — but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was “only kidding.” The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday, and Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room. “So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?” Trump said. “Thank you for the offer, sir — for the offer, I have no, no — I do not want to be in politics,” White replied. Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: “I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody.” The press secretary’s post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job. Trump’s announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to “violent Fighter and Warrior” White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party’s stunning midterm elections defeat. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year. But there was also some skepticism about the president’s announcement, and Trump said Sunday night that he had been joking. – ‘Beat the hell out of you’ – Leading out White to the podium on Monday, Trump said he had been “having a little fun.” “He’s a great guy,” Trump told the room full of reporters. “The only problem is he’ll talk for a little while and then he’s going to beat the hell out of you.” Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon — the ring used for UFC fights. “I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” he joked — before quickliy adding: “I have zero political aspirations.” White added that “the last 24 hours of my life has been insane” since Trump made the announcement. Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, White added: “I don’t tell the president ‘no’ to anything… I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.” Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang. nigeria.title: N10m reward to motivate FCT councillors, not vote buying — APC chair defends Wike
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Nentawe Yilwatda, has defended the N10 million reward promised by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to councillors who deliver their wards for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, on Monday, Yilwatda said the money was intended to motivate councillors and would be paid after the election, once the result had been established. “He was speaking to the FCT councillors in the forum, and I’m sure it’s addressing something about 62 or 60-something councillors in the FCT,” he said. Asked whether the offer amounted to voter inducement, Yilwatda rejected the suggestion, arguing that political parties routinely provide funds for mobilisation. “Which political party doesn’t release money for mobilisation? Which political party? So, tell me one. No, it’s not for votes. The same reward for you to deliver Tinubu in your ward,” he said. Yilwatda compared the offer to rewarding students for academic achievement but maintained that the timing of the payment was significant. “The money is not given before the election. It doesn’t matter? No, it matters. It matters because if the money is given after the election has been concluded and the winner has been declared and there’s nothing at stake again—if the court has proven and all the legal rules have been followed—that you legally deliver your ward by giving you N10 million,” he said. Asked again whether he considered the offer of vote buying, Yilwatda replied authoritatively: “Never.” Wike made the pledge at a political meeting in Kwali Area Council, promising N10 million to each councillor who delivers their ward for Tinubu and the APC in 2027. Asked whether the APC would return Godswill Akpabio as Senate President if he wins re-election, Yilwatda said the decision would rest with senators. “Let’s wait for the election first. I don’t have anybody in mind. The Senate will determine who they want to make the Senate President,” he said. On reports of electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, Yilwatda said he sympathised with anyone injured and said the APC supported free and fair elections. “If anybody is injured by anybody across the country, I’m sure it shouldn’t be by APC supporters. I pity anybody who is being injured, and I sympathise with them. Our party stands for free and fair elections,” he said. nigeria.title: Trump sees ‘positive momentum’ on Iran after Qatar PM talks
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was momentum toward ending the war with Iran, as he declared that the country “militarily, is effectively over,” but kept open the possibility of new strikes. Trump met at the White House with Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani — a key mediator in the Iran war. It was his first meeting with a foreign leader since his party’s massive losses in the midterm elections. Trump later posted on Truth Social that the two leaders had “an excellent conversation” and that “much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran.” In the weeks leading up to the midterms, there was widespread speculation that US strikes against Iran would resume soon after. However, Trump has talked down resuming the conflict while leaving the door open to further strikes — a position he reiterated Monday at a White House press briefing. “Iran, militarily, is effectively over. We’re just keeping it the status quo,” Trump told reporters. “But if we do have to go back in, we are locked and loaded, and ready to go.” In his social post on Monday, Trump said that he believed further strikes were “quite unlikely” given that key US allies in the Gulf “would prefer the status quo.” “We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said. – ‘Imaginary talks’ – Iranian officials meanwhile expressed defiance at the continued pressure from Washington. The Islamic republic’s top security chief, Mohsen Rezai, wrote on X late Monday that the US “flails like a desperate gambler,” telling Washington to “fold your hand. Stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks.” Earlier, Tehran’s top negotiator Mahammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed on X that Israel was pushing the US deeper into conflict, adding that “unless Washington drops the ‘Israel First’ mindset, America and its allies are headed straight for a dark age.” On the ground in Iran, strikes — which have not been publicly acknowledged by the US military — are continuing, according to Iranian authorities. The island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, was targeted overnight from Sunday to Monday, the provincial deputy governor stated on state television. Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat, not least because it has contributed to rising prices in the US economy. nigeria.title: I give kudos to people who sent me to jail; it’s like school – Orji Kalu
nigeria.description: Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has praised those responsible for his imprisonment, saying the six months he spent behind bars gave him valuable life lessons and made him a more humble person. Kalu said rather than regret his incarceration, he considers it an experience that changed his understanding of life and helped him develop a different outlook. The former Abia State governor made the remarks during an interview on Arise Television on Monday. Explaining why he was grateful for the experience, Kalu said, “It made me more humble. It made me to realise that life is not the same thing I used to think about. So I’m very grateful to God I was there.” He added, “And I gave kudos to people that sent me there because it’s like going to school. And I graduated there, and I’m very happy I went there.” Kalu was convicted by a Federal High Court in Lagos in December 2019 on a 39-count charge and sentenced to 12 years’ imprisonment. However, the Supreme Court overturned the conviction on May 8, 2020, ruling that the trial judge, Mohammed Idris, lacked jurisdiction to deliver the judgment after his elevation to the Court of Appeal. The apex court ordered a fresh trial, and Kalu was released from Kuje Correctional Centre after spending approximately six months in custody. Asked whether he believed the conviction was justified, the senator disagreed but said he did not wish to dwell on the matter. “No, it wasn’t the right thing to do. But I don’t like to discuss this because the judge had his reasons. When the judge did it, I praised him. I support all his decisions,” he said. Kalu also acknowledged that the judiciary had its challenges but maintained that some judges remained committed to dispensing justice. He advised Nigerians dissatisfied with rulings of lower courts to pursue appeals rather than publicly condemn judicial decisions. According to him, taking cases to higher courts gives litigants another opportunity to obtain justice, as more judges are involved in reviewing the decisions. Speaking with AFP, Torero said both rain and drought can impact harvests and production of crops for animal feed. Floods can be particularly devastating, destroying stored food and damaging the infrastructure and transportation needed to get products to market. All these elements can push up prices, and the impacts “can emerge well before harvests are completed,” he said. “Markets react to expectations of future shortages and uncertainty itself can generate volatility,” he told AFP. This year’s El Niño impacts are exacerbated by price shocks caused by the war in Iran, which have raised the cost of fuel and fertiliser for farmers and impacted household spending globally. “For vulnerable households, even moderate food price increases can have huge consequences,” said Torero. “Poor families spend a large share of their incomes on food and therefore have limited capacity to absorb price shocks and spikes,” he added. The consequences can include reduced food consumption, poorer quality diets and “ultimately, increased food insecurity and malnutrition,” he said. In September, the FAO said it had received just one-fifth of the $202 million it requested to prepare for an El Niño-linked food crisis in 22 high-risk countries. nigeria.title: I sold heavy weapons internationally – Orji Kalu
nigeria.description: …Says he sold arms to anyone who could buy The Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has disclosed that he previously engaged in the international trade of heavy weapons, selling arms to buyers in different countries before quitting the business at the insistence of his parents. Kalu made the revelation during an interview on Arise Television on Monday, while discussing his business background and relationships with former and current South African leaders. Asked whether he was an arms dealer, the former Abia State governor answered in the affirmative, saying he stopped after his parents intervened. “Yes, so I stopped because my parents, my mother, my father came and said I must stop, and I stopped,” he said. Asked whether he sold weapons to people who intended to use them to kill others, Kalu dismissed the suggestion, saying his motivation was to make money. “No, no, no, no, no, no. I was selling guns to make money, whether they blow up it’s not my business,” he said. The interviewer subsequently asked whether he supplied weapons to the African National Congress (ANC) during its struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Kalu said he did not restrict his business to the ANC, explaining that he sold weapons to any buyer who could afford them. “No, I was selling to anybody who wants to buy. Asked about the source of the weapons, the senator declined to provide details, saying, “It’s only my business.” The interviewer also questioned how his former arms trade related to Nigeria’s current security challenges and the proliferation of small arms. In response, Kalu clarified that the weapons he traded were not small arms but heavy weapons sold between countries. “No, these are heavy arms that were sold country to country,” he said. Asked specifically whether he sold weapons to Libya under its late leader, Muammar Gaddafi, Kalu said he sold to anyone with the financial capacity to purchase them. “To anybody that had money to buy,” he responded. nigeria.title: 2027: Most Christians we’ve engaged are okay with Muslim-Muslim ticket – Yilwatda
nigeria.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, says most Christians consulted by the party have expressed satisfaction with the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 general elections. Yilwatda said Christians’ initial concerns that the arrangement could marginalise them had not materialised, insisting that their voices remained represented in the administration. The APC chairman stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. “Most Christians that we’ve engaged and we’ve spoken to them, they are very okay with the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he said. “The thought and the fear of most Christians was that the Muslim-Muslim ticket may suppress their voices, but their voices are heard loud and clear now.” He also dismissed concerns that Tinubu’s religion had exposed Christians to discrimination or persecution during his three years in office. On questions surrounding the President’s health and fitness to contest the 2027 election, Yilwatda maintained that Tinubu was physically capable of seeking re-election. He also defended the President’s decision not to attend every campaign rally, arguing that his constitutional responsibilities would not allow him to participate in all party engagements. According to him, some government officials have been advised to attend selected rallies to ensure that governance is not affected by campaign activities. On the leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Yilwatda denied allegations that the APC was behind the party’s internal dispute following the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the David Mark-led leadership. He questioned the opposition party’s decision to blame the ruling party over a dispute arising from a legal action instituted by one of its members. The APC chairman further expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in a free and fair election. He attributed Atiku’s performance in the 2023 presidential election largely to the political structure of the Peoples Democratic Party rather than his personal popularity. “He did not win because of Atiku; he won because of the structure of the PDP. It was the PDP that brought Atiku, not Atiku winning on his own,” Yilwatda said. He also defended FCT Minister Nyesom Wike’s proposed ₦10m reward for councils that deliver their wards for Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the incentive did not constitute vote buying. nigeria.title: Edo LGA orders daily bush surveillance ahead of Yuletide

Ekpeson, who is also the Edo State Chairman of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON), gave the directive during an emergency security meeting with vigilante leaders and coordinators to address security concerns ahead of the festive season. A statement issued on Monday, November 9, 2026, by Agbukor Lucky Apeakhuye, the chairman’s media aide on Politics and Strategic Development, said the meeting focused on strengthening security operations across Etsako East. According to the statement, Ekpeson directed vigilante operatives to conduct daily surveillance and thoroughly comb bushes, forests and identified security flashpoints to prevent criminal elements from using remote locations as hideouts. The chairman warned that kidnapping, killings, cult-related activities, violence and other criminal acts would not be tolerated anywhere in the local government area. He also charged security coordinators to strengthen intelligence gathering, improve collaboration among their teams and ensure adequate security coverage across communities throughout the festive period. Those at the meeting included the Vice Chairman, Comrade Charles Aloaye Dagana; Secretary to the Local Government, Dr. Samuel Oshiole Enaboakpe; and Chief Adolphus Oshole Osimi, General Officer Commanding of the Agenebode Zonal Vigilante Command, who oversees security operations across villages in the Weppa-Wanno axis. Other vigilante coordinators also attended the meeting. The statement said Ekpeson reiterated that the protection of lives and property remained a priority of his administration, urging security operatives to remain vigilant, proactive and responsive to distress calls. He further charged vigilante leaders to ensure that the directives translated into concrete action, saying he would not want reports of kidnapping, killings, cult-related violence or other criminal activities across the local government. The meeting, according to the statement, formed part of the council’s measures to strengthen security and ensure peaceful Christmas and New Year celebrations in Etsako East. nigeria.title: FG unveils N70bn plan to tackle Noma
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has unveiled a N70bn National Oral Health Strategic Plan for 2026–2030 to improve access to dental care, address the burden of oral diseases and eliminate Noma as a public health problem. The five-year plan is designed to expand preventive and curative oral health services, improve early detection and treatment of Noma, strengthen the dental workforce and integrate oral healthcare into primary healthcare services across the 774 local government areas. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, announced the initiative on Monday in Abuja during the commemoration of National Noma Day and National Oral Health Day. According to a statement by the ministry’s Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Ado Bako, Salako said the initiative aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises the health and wellbeing of Nigerians. He described oral health as a critical component of Universal Health Coverage, saying it should no longer be neglected in the country’s healthcare delivery system. Expressing concern over Nigeria’s burden of Noma, particularly in the North-West and North-East, the minister described the disease as preventable but devastating, with the potential to cause severe facial disfigurement, disability and death, especially among malnourished children. He said the World Health Organisation’s recognition of Noma as a Neglected Tropical Disease in 2023 marked a significant milestone in global efforts to combat the condition. Salako disclosed that the Federal Ministry of Health had integrated Noma surveillance into the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system, while intensifying efforts to improve early detection and referral through primary healthcare facilities. He added that frontline health workers, traditional healers and traditional birth attendants had been trained in 19 states to identify early signs of Noma and other oral diseases and facilitate prompt referrals for treatment. Highlighting gaps in oral healthcare delivery, the minister said more than 80 per cent of Nigerians had never visited a dentist, while two out of every three children were living with untreated dental caries. He further disclosed that Nigeria had approximately one dentist for every 38,000 people, compared with the World Health Organisation’s recommended ratio of one dentist to 7,500 people. To address the challenges, Salako said the government was strengthening the integration of oral healthcare into primary healthcare through the Sector-Wide Approach and the Basic Health Care Provision Fund to improve access to affordable and quality services. nigeria.title: China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria!
nigeria.description: I came looking for ancient soldiers and left thinking about Nigeria’s tourism potential! One of the things I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures and, of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepares you for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! For anyone who has watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there! But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to around 221 BC, when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that! While some people prepare for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation! The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. And what makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over two thousand years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974, when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army! I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. UNESCO designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. But beyond the fascinating history, what struck me most was what China has done with this discovery. This is where the story becomes particularly interesting for Nigeria. China has not simply uncovered an ancient treasure and left it to gather dust. It has invested in archaeological research, conservation, restoration, museum infrastructure, visitor facilities and tourism development. The preservation work itself is remarkable. entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. sports.title: How Eagles can use their growing collection of premium NFL draft picks
sports.description: The Eagles have created options with their draft capital. What they do with those options will determine whether their deadline decisions improve the organization. Following the Jordan Davis agreement, Philadelphia holds five first-round picks and five second-round picks across the next three drafts, according to Jeff McLane’s reported inventory. That matches Adam Schefter’s total of 10 selections in the first two rounds. The collection gives Howie Roseman several paths. None requires announcing a target, predicting a specific draft position, or deciding today how to use every pick. Make multiple selections at premium positions The most direct approach is to draft players. Multiple early selections let Philadelphia address more than one need without relying on later-round prospects to fill immediate openings. The Eagles can evaluate offensive line, defensive line, and other positions based on available talent. Their draft capital should support that evaluation rather than force a predetermined shopping list. Selecting well also creates the possibility of productive players on rookie contracts, helping balance spending elsewhere. Move within a draft when the value supports it Additional selections let Philadelphia move up for a player it values or move down when another team offers worthwhile compensation. That flexibility should not become a trade requirement. Keeping a selection can be the best decision when a strong prospect remains available. The important advantage is having alternatives when the board develops differently than expected. Trade for an established contributor Premium picks can acquire players with an NFL track record. That may become attractive if Philadelphia identifies a specific roster weakness and believes the player’s age, contract, and performance fit its competitive plans. The cost includes more than the pick. An established acquisition can require a substantial contract, limiting the financial advantage of retaining draft choices. Any such move should be tied to a defined need and a realistic assessment of the roster. Spread investment across several years Philadelphia’s early selections are distributed across 2027, 2028, and 2029. That allows the organization to address needs as they evolve rather than concentrating every decision in one offseason. Keep the focus on development Acquiring selections is only part of roster building. Philadelphia must create an environment in which those players can improve, earn responsibilities, and become dependable starters. The Davis trade increased flexibility. It did not guarantee the next successful roster. That will require disciplined decisions, effective coaching, and patience with players whose development will not follow a straight line. sports.title: Laura Stegall taught her daughter to play volleyball - and a lot more about how to fight
sports.description: INDIANAPOLIS — Laura Stegall is somewhere amid the sea of blue that's overtaken half the lower bowl at Gainbridge Fieldhouse Saturday night. She's sporting blue-and-white checkered overalls, celebrating the now three-time defending Class 4A state champion Fort Wayne Carroll volleyball team's four-set win over Center Grove with her son, Brady. Down on the floor, Laura's daughters — senior outside hitter Sarah and freshman setter Ashtyn — are posing for a photo with their dad, Carroll assistant athletic director Randy Stegall. Sarah credits both her parents with "setting the standard" in her life. But her love for volleyball was inspired by Laura, who was a two-sport athlete at Indiana Purdue Fort Wayne (basketball), then launched college volleyball programs at Indiana Tech and Daytona State (Fla.). Laura was Sarah's first coach, the one who taught the Notre Dame commit everything she knows. The two text about the sport on a near-daily basis, Sarah says. "She gets a message before every game, whether she wants it or not," Laura adds in a separate interview. My mom wants the best for me, to make sure I'm always playing with confidence, Sarah explains from outside Gainbridge, the blue championship medal draped around her neck and Laura standing proudly alongside her. The odds were stacked against Laura living to see her oldest child reach high school, let alone play out her senior season. Laura was diagnosed with late-stage ovarian cancer in February 2019. She was given a 39% chance of living five years and a 20% of making it a decade. "But by the grace of God, I'm here eight years later," Laura said in a phone interview with IndyStar last week. Sarah was her family's bedrock while her mother underwent cancer treatments. Just nine years old at the time, she took charge at home, cooking meals and looking after her siblings so Laura could rest while Randy, a college baseball coach at the time, was on the road. "Sarah's truly one of the most responsible, mature people and she stepped up so majorly for our family," Laura says before being overwhelmed by her emotions. "That's a lot to ask of a 9-year-old: 'Hey, I need you to do this for your brother. I need you to cook dinner,' but Sarah stepped up — and she still cooks better than me." Laura takes a moment to collect herself, then reflects on one of her favorite sports memories with Sarah, a swim meet back when the family still lived in Florida. Laura had recently completed cancer treatments and was in attendance to see her 10-year old daughter break a 28-year old breaststroke record. It was a "euphoric moment," she says, her pride beaming through the phone. "And every little benchmark along the way. … I'm sitting there watching Sarah like, 'I'm so grateful to be here to see this.'" 'Mom, are you gonna die?' sports.description: Jim Harbaugh © Imagn. The Los Angeles Chargers remain winless after eight games as questions grow around head coach Jim Harbaugh. On his podcast 3 & OUT with John Middlekauff , the analyst compared Harbaugh with former Chargers head coach Brandon Staley, who was fired in his third season. “1, 2, 3, trade me, please. 1, 2, 3, we quit. 1, 2, 3, this is worse than Brandon Staley,” Middlekauff said. “If Jim Harbaugh’s name was Jim Middlekauff, I think he probably would’ve already been fired. sports.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Over the years, there have been a lot of complaints about the rising cost of attending an NBA game, but fans in Texas were offered incredible get-in prices for Monday’s slate of games. With three NBA teams, Texas is the state that boasts the second-most franchises, only behind California with four. All three teams have exciting, big-name superstars and playoff aspirations. But you would never know that, going by the ticket prices they were charging for games on Monday night. Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks had incredibly low get-in prices for Monday night games According to data from TickPick , the Houston Rockets vs. Denver Nuggets had a staggeringly low get-in price of just $10 hours before tip-off. As for the Dallas Mavericks, who hosted the Indiana Pacers (albeit without Tyrese Haliburton), they offered fans a get-in price of just $14. These get-in ticket prices actually cost less than the average cost of a six-wing meal combo at WingStop, which only goes to show how affordable the deal was for fans. And while going through first- or third-party ticketing platforms would have added some fees to the overall price of the order, NBA fans in Texas would still be getting a very good deal given the average price of NBA tickets elsewhere in the country and the superstars that were playing. The get-in price of the Rockets vs. Nuggets game is especially surprising, as it boasted two all-time great superstars in Nikola Jokic and Kevin Durant. With a superstar pairing that boasts four MVPs, three NBA championships, and three Finals MVPs between them, you would imagine the demand for tickets would be much higher. technology.description: Microsoft is retiring its free education email service, leaving schools, colleges, and universities facing new licensing bills if they want to keep students' mailboxes. The company announced plans last week to retire Office 365 A1, the Student Use Benefit program, and free Exchange Online for Alumni. The changes generally take effect at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Office 365 A1 provides eligible institutions with web-based Office applications, Teams, and email at no charge. Its replacement, Microsoft 365 Education A0, excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also depends on paid faculty licensing and students actively using Windows devices for education. A spokesperson for the UK's Department for Education told The Register : "We are disappointed that Microsoft has made this decision. However, we are pleased to have successfully negotiated some additional concessions for the UK, giving schools, colleges and universities the time they need to be able to successfully transition to new licensing agreements." An industry insider said the loss of free Microsoft-hosted email could add thousands to institutions' bills. Another organization noted "significant concerns… around affordability, equitable treatment across the sector, and the longer-term implications of the changes." A spokesperson for UK education technology body Jisc told The Register that its "focus has been on ensuring that UK education providers are well supported and have sufficient time to assess their options." "We continue working closely with Microsoft and sector partners to support those discussions and help institutions make informed decisions about their future requirements." Also being retired are free Exchange Online for Alumni - which lets graduates retain their mailboxes - and the Student Use Benefit, providing student licenses at no additional charge when institutions purchase qualifying faculty licenses. Microsoft plans a paid alumni replacement. The Windows giant is also changing storage entitlements and introducing Microsoft 365 Education A7, its "most advanced education offering," which adds AI, security, governance, and device-management features. Asked why it was removing those services from the free tier, Microsoft framed the overhaul as a response to institutions' changing needs. A spokesperson told The Register : "Education institutions are evaluating AI, security, privacy, governance, and teaching and learning as connected priorities rather than separate technology decisions. technology.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
technology.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. The product has become particularly useful since Anthropic's Mythos model, and similar AI offerings, made it possible to quickly find more software bugs and flaws and overwhelmed tech teams whose patching apparatus was not set up to handle hundreds of montly CVEs. Live Protect currently works on some of Cisco's datacenter switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. "Expect this to be a major investment area," Schultz added. ®

technology.title: Anthropic's super bug-finding Mythos model is going into Cisco and IBM products
technology.description: Anthropic has started extending access to its bug-finding Mythos model by allowing Cisco and IBM to make it part of their security products. Cisco announced its integration today at an event in Melbourne, Australia, where it revealed that the red teaming tools in its AI Defense suite, which looks for weaknesses and inappropriate activity in AI models, agents, and applications they power, will be able to call Mythos to test customers’ setups. “At a very high level, AI Defense has the ability to look at models and break them,” said Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing. He said the tool is now “super-charged by Mythos” and will identify more danger that AI Defense will then address. AI Defense already uses AI-powered red teaming to find flaws. Mythos will become another option. Cisco will make it available under users’ existing licenses, without additional cost. Natalie Mead, Anthropic’s head of applied AI for the Asia-Pacific, said the company has a long queue of buyers who want to use Mythos, and working with Cisco will make it easier to satisfy that demand. Anthropic initially made Mythos available under "Project Glasswing," a program that gave vetted organizations access to the model to test their codebases, but has since expanded access through other controlled programs, an arrangement that makes considerable sense because in the wrong hands Mythos could help attackers exploit software flaws. The Cisco deal exposes the functionality of Mythos to end-users, without letting them use the model itself. The Register asked Mead if Anthropic has similar deals with other third parties and she demurred. That may be because a few hours after Cisco told us about its use of Mythos, IBM announced that it will also integrate Anthropic’s model into a product – namely its Concert tool, which uses AI to scan applications for risks and weaknesses. IBM says it will use Mythos “to uncover weaknesses traditional scanners miss, determine which pose real risk and generate fixes for developer approval.” We have asked Anthropic if these integrations represent a decision to open Mythos to more users in more ways. We will update this story if we receive a substantial response. Also on Monday, Anthropic introduced version 5.2 of Mythos and Fable, which the company says generate outputs up to 30 percent faster than version 5.1 yet cost less: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Users can choose to run both models in “fast mode,” which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times, and doubles prices to $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens. science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of elements. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos “It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun , director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time . The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. science.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029 , when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo . Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. science.title: NYT bestseller ‘Robopocalypse’ is getting a TV series with Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman at the helm
science.description: null They say all good things come to those who wait… and WAIT. Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. It does seem like an eternity since news first broke that Portland-based New York Times bestselling author Daniel H. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay. That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required. But now we have been blessed with the news , first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. And what timing, just as AI fever has gripped the planet with paranoia centered around our eventual robot overlords. "'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and suspense of a major action story, but what drew me to it are the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its center," Ron Howard shared in a statement. science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. The luminous blue variable and supernova impostor AT 2016blu is in the middle of the small square. X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said.
